compliance: Listed on CITES Appendix II (all Cycadaceae not in Appendix I); international trade needs permits, UK-grown nursery stock does not.
foliage: evergreen; stiff, glossy, pinnate dark green fronds with sharp-tipped leaflets
hardinessNote: Half-hardy, approximately -5 to 1°C; keep dry and protect from hard frost in winter.
pollination: not applicable; a dioecious cycad that bears cones rather than flowers, grown for foliage
prune: Remove dead or yellowed fronds at the base with secateurs. Wear gloves, as the leaflet tips are sharp.
resilience: Tolerates dry air and short dry spells; damaged by frost and cold wet compost. Pests: scale insects and mealybugs, especially indoors.
toxicity: Highly toxic: all parts, especially the seeds, can be fatal if eaten, causing liver failure. Children, dogs and cats are at risk, and dogs are frequently poisoned.
uncertain: hardiness: RHS H3 (sheltered); draft said H2. Nurseries quote -4 to -7°C if kept dry
size: RHS 1–1.5 m over 20–50 years; Burncoose 2 m, Hardy Tropicals up to 6 m in the wild
light: RHS lists partial shade as preferred, so sunNeed lowered 75 -> 60, sunMin 40 -> 30
compliance: Appendix II from CITES documents and secondary lists; C. revoluta not found in Appendix I; check the CITES checklist for changes
toxicity: cycasin; seeds most toxic; dvm360 gives 32% mortality in dogs showing signs
clay: judged no because it needs sharp drainage
uses: Conservatory · houseplant · patio pots moved under cover for winter · exotic summer displays
visual: Rosette of stiff glossy dark green feather-like fronds on a stout shaggy trunk · year-round foliage · very slow
water: Water when the top of the compost dries in summer; keep almost dry in winter, never letting water sit in the crown.
